Subject: POC: Prompt Review Workshop — calendar coordination & load-test window

Hi Sergio / Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week. The product and latency numbers looked promising — the team is excited to move into a short POC.

We'd like to schedule a hands-on workshop focused on:
- Prompt inventory & categorization (intent mapping / structured outputs)
- Routing and guardrails (safety & hallucination mitigation)
- A short load-test to validate throughput & latency at our typical qps

Proposed slots (PDT):
- Tue 19 May 10:00–11:30
- Wed 20 May 14:00–15:30
- Thu 21 May 09:00–10:30

Attendees from our side: Anna Kaplan (product), Rajesh Kumar (eng lead), Maya Li (SRE). We'll be prepared to share a prompt sample set. Could you confirm your suggested Redwood attendees and whether you can run a light load test (100–200 qps sustained for 10m) during/after the session?

Also: would you prefer a 90-minute interactive workshop or two shorter sessions?

I've attached a quick POC expectations doc (attached: poc_scope.pdf) — feel free to add to it.

Best,
Anna

Anna — thanks for the clear agenda, this looks great.

We recommend a single 90-minute hands-on workshop so we can do the prompt inventory live and finish with a short load test. Proposed Redwood attendees: Monica Patel (Solutions Engineer, will lead prompt/guardrail work), Dev Patel (Infra, will run load-test & collect metrics), and myself to run the session and align on next steps.

We can cover the following deliverables by the end of the workshop:
- Annotated prompt inventory (mapping to intents + output schema)
- Guardrail checklist and example templates for structured outputs
- Short load-test sweep with baseline latency/cost metrics

Our availability aligns with your Tue/Wed/Thu slots. My preference is Tue 19 May 10:00–11:30 PDT. If that works for you we'll send a calendar invite and a brief agenda.

One ask before the session: can you upload a sample prompt inventory (CSV/XLSX) and any existing routing rules to a shared Drive so Monica can prepare specific examples? Also please confirm the model profile — will you want to test an open LLM we host or a customer-provided model in your VPC?

Thanks, looking forward.

— Sergio
